items.title: Timelike worldlines, proper time, length and four-velocity on a Lorentzian four-manifold
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the coordinate representative and its derivatives through order $k$
  are continuous up to $t_0$ on the relative interval
  $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$, with derivatives at
  $t_0$ taken one-sided. For $k=\infty$ this holds at every finite order.
  Merely possessing a one-sided secant tangent, as defined next, does not
  by itself make a curve $C^1$ at the endpoint. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $[s_{i-1},s_i]$ is $C^1$ up to its included
  endpoints in the one-sided sense above: in every endpoint chart its
  component derivatives on the open piece have continuous one-sided limits,
  agreeing with its endpoint derivatives. Equivalently each piece has a
  $C^1$ extension to its closed parameter piece. In particular its right
  tangent at $s_{i-1}$ and left tangent at $s_i$ exist. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. The piece extensions give continuity at the
  corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the velocity derivation of
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] translated to the parameter
value $t$. In a chart around $\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** A **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The continuous one-sided limits of the component derivatives, required
by the $C^1$ extension of each piece, and continuity of $g$ imply that
$h_i$ tends to the norm of the corresponding endpoint tangent. The future
timelike hypothesis on those tangents makes these limits strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
the function with $\tau(s_0)=0$ and $\tau(s)$ equal to the increment
from $s_0$ to $s$ when $s>s_0$, and minus the increment from $s$ to $s_0$
when $s<s_0$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.
items.strategy: Define future timelike worldlines as piecewise-C^1 curves with future timelike one-sided tangents, proper time by the density sqrt(-g(gamma',gamma'))/c, and the four-velocity as the unit tangent; fix the SI unit and coordinate conventions imported from the framework page.

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 2.2 (2.4)-(2.9) and section 2.3 (2.14) on proper time and the four-velocity, printed pp. 27-30 (PDF pp. 28-31)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), sections 1.1.1-1.1.2 on the particle action, the affine parameter and the four-velocity, printed pp. 24-30 (PDF pp. 31-37)

items.title: Proper time is well defined and reparametrization invariant; the four-velocity is its unit tangent
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$c>0$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

1. **Well-definedness and additivity of proper time.** Let
   $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike worldline
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]). Then the sum defining
   $\tau(b)-\tau(a)$ is the same for every admissible partition of $[a,b]$; it
   is written $\frac1c\int_a^b h$, where $h$ is the piecewise-defined
   proper-time density. For $a<c<b$,
   $\tau(b)-\tau(a)=\bigl(\tau(c)-\tau(a)\bigr)+\bigl(\tau(b)-\tau(c)\bigr)$.
   If $a<b$, the increment is strictly positive.

2. **Reparametrization and orientation, including subintervals.** Let
   $a'<b'$ and let $\varphi:[a',b']\to[a,b]$ be $C^1$ up to its included
   endpoints with nonzero derivative everywhere, including one-sided endpoint
   derivatives. Let $\tilde\gamma:=\gamma\circ\varphi$. Its derivative has
   constant sign and $\varphi$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto its actual image
   interval. If $\varphi'>0$, then $\tilde\gamma$ is a piecewise-$C^1$ future
   timelike worldline and
   $$\tilde\tau(b')-\tilde\tau(a')=\tau(\varphi(b'))-\tau(\varphi(a')).$$
   This equals $\tau(b)-\tau(a)$ when $\varphi(a')=a$ and $\varphi(b')=b$.
   If $\varphi'<0$, then $\tilde\gamma$ is a piecewise-$C^1$ **past** timelike
   traversal. Its unsigned density
   $\tilde h=\sqrt{-g(\tilde\gamma',\tilde\gamma')}$ obeys
   $$\frac1c\int_{a'}^{b'}\tilde h=\tau(\varphi(a'))-\tau(\varphi(b'))>0,$$
   whereas the oriented original difference
   $\tau(\varphi(b'))-\tau(\varphi(a'))$ is negative. For endpoint-reversing
   $\varphi(a')=b$, $\varphi(b')=a$, the latter equals
   $-\bigl(\tau(b)-\tau(a)\bigr)$. This negative oriented difference is not
   elapsed proper time for a future curve; parameter reversal reverses the
   causal direction. Non-surjective maps compare increments over their
   actual image interval, not over the whole original interval.

3. **Proper-time function and four-velocity.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a
   $C^1$ future timelike worldline on an interval with nonempty interior and
   let $\tau$ be its proper-time function based at $t_0\in I$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]). Then $\tau$ is $C^1$ on
   $I$ with
   $$\tau'(t)=\frac{1}{c}\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}>0,$$
   so $\tau$ is strictly increasing, and at every $t\in I$ the velocity,
   proper-time density and four-velocity satisfy
   $\gamma'(t)=\tau'(t)\,U(t)$ and $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$. If
   $\tau$ is strictly increasing on $I$ with image $J$, then the
   reparametrized curve $\gamma_\tau:=\gamma\circ(\tau|_I)^{-1}$ is a $C^1$
   future timelike worldline on $J$ with
   $$\gamma_\tau'(\sigma)=U\bigl(\tau^{-1}(\sigma)\bigr),\qquad g\bigl(\gamma_\tau'(\sigma),\gamma_\tau'(\sigma)\bigr)=-c^2 .$$
   The same formulas hold piece by piece for a piecewise-$C^1$ future
   timelike worldline, on each open piece and at its endpoints one-sided, with the two
   corner velocities kept distinct.
items.strategy: Use standard C1 closed-piece extensions, finite refinement and Darboux additivity; compare increments over each parameter map's actual image interval, distinguish future increasing reparametrization from past reversal, and prove interior and one-sided endpoint inverse derivatives and four-velocity normalization.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the metric-selected connection of a nondegenerate metric, and its extension to tensor fields
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$
items.strategy: Construct the metric-selected connection by the Koszul form 2g(nabla_X Y,Z)=K(X,Y,Z), prove torsion freedom and metric compatibility from the defining identities, derive uniqueness, and extend the derivative to dual and tensor fields with commuting contraction and vanishing on g and g^{-1}.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 3.2: the theorem, the Koszul-type derivation (3.23)-(3.29) and the Christoffel formula (3.31)-(3.33), printed pp. 35-37 (PDF pp. 36-38)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3 'covariant derivatives and connections': metric compatibility (3.19) and the Christoffel-symbol solution (3.21)-(3.23), printed pp. 59-61 (PDF pp. 66-68); covariant derivatives of one-forms and tensors (3.13)-(3.15), printed pp. 57-58 (PDF pp. 64-65)
D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.2.3 and equation (3.17), printed pp. 109-111 (PDF pp. 116-118)

items.title: Covariant differentiation along curves: metric pairing, parallel transport and geodesic speed
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.

3. **Geodesic speed and affine parameter.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the norm
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')$ is constant, so the causal character of $\gamma$
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant on $I$; a nonzero constant value
   makes $\gamma$ regular on all of $I$. If $\gamma$ is timelike and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then the proper-time
   increment of $\gamma$ over $[t_0,t]$ is $\lambda(t-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter of $\gamma$; the four-velocity
   $U=\lambda^{-1}\gamma'$ is parallel, $D_\tau U=0$ in the proper-time
   parameter. A null geodesic has $g(\gamma',\gamma')=0$ and admits no
   proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic and let
   $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto its open image with $h'\neq0$.
   Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and only if $h(s)=as+b$ with
   constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the constant
   $h'$, and every affine parameter of $\gamma$ arises in this way from a
   fixed one.
items.strategy: Prove the metric pairing identity for the covariant derivative along curves, existence and uniqueness of parallel sections and the metric-preserving transport map, constancy of geodesic speed, proper time as an affine parameter, and the affine-reparametrization criterion.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: the equation of parallel transport (3.31) printed p. 65 (PDF p. 72); geodesics (3.47) and the affine parameter, printed pp. 70-71 (PDF pp. 77-78); 'parallel transport with respect to a metric-compatible connection preserves inner products' (3.33)-(3.34), printed pp. 66-67 (PDF pp. 73-74)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 3.3: the exercise that $g(X,X)$ is constant along a geodesic, the free-particle postulate and the remark on proper time as an affine parameter, printed p. 38 (PDF p. 39)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.3.1: $\nabla_Xg=0$ implies that parallely transported vectors keep their angle with the geodesic tangent, printed p. 119 (PDF p. 126)

items.title: The geodesic initial-value problem and the exponential map of the metric-selected connection
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.
items.strategy: Solve the geodesic system in charts by Picard-Lindelof with smooth dependence on parameters, glue chart solutions into a unique maximal geodesic, prove openness of the flow domain and the scaling relation, and construct the exponential map with d(exp_p)_0 = id.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 3.3-3.4: the geodesic theorem, the exponential map and normal coordinates, printed pp. 37-40 (PDF pp. 38-41)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3 'geodesics' (3.47), (3.62)-(3.63): the geodesic equation, its affine freedom and the exponential map, printed pp. 70-73 (PDF pp. 77-80)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.3.1-3.3.2: geodesics revisited, affine parametrization, the exponential map and normal coordinates, printed pp. 119-121 (PDF pp. 126-128)

items.title: Point-normal and exponential coordinate charts of the metric-selected connection
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose geodesics
and exponential map are those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Point-normal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there is a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ such that, in the components of this chart,

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0,\qquad \partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}.$$

The construction starts from any chart around $p$ and is finite: no frame field
on $U$ and no global trivialization of $TM$ is used.

**(b) Exponential charts.** For every $p\in M$ and every $g_p$-orthonormal
basis $e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$ there is a star-shaped open neighborhood
$W\subseteq T_pM$ of $0$ on which $\exp_p$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open
$U_p\ni p$, and the chart

$$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U_p\longrightarrow\mathbb R^4,$$

where $\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ is the coordinate isomorphism of the basis,
satisfies $u(p)=0$ and the same three normal-form identities at $p$ as in (a).
Moreover every geodesic through $p$ has, in the chart $u$, the form
$u(\gamma(t))=t\,k$ for a constant $k\in\mathbb R^4$, as long as it remains in
$U_p$; in particular the geodesics through $p$ are the coordinate lines
through the origin. No assertion is made about the second derivatives of the
metric at $p$: the construction is first order and does not make a neighborhood
of $p$ isometric to Minkowski space.
items.strategy: Construct the point-normal chart exp_p o psi^{-1} to obtain g_{ab}(p)=eta_{ab}, partial g(p)=0 and Gamma(p)=0, construct exponential charts in which the geodesics through p are the straight coordinate lines, and record that no second-order vanishing is claimed.

items.title: First variation of the length of a timelike curve: stationarity is the geodesic equation
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $a<b$, and
let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve whose image is
contained in the domain $U$ of one smooth chart $(U,x)$
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]). Suppose $\gamma$ is
parametrized so that

$$g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)=-c^2 \qquad (t\in[a,b]),$$

that is, by proper time up to a choice of origin
([[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]). Let
$H:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times[a,b]\to U$ be a map that is $C^2$ in both
variables, with $H(0,t)=\gamma(t)$ for all $t$, with
$H(s,a)=\gamma(a)$ and $H(s,b)=\gamma(b)$ for all $s$, and such that each
curve $t\mapsto H(s,t)$ is future timelike; write
$T(s,t):=\partial_tH(s,t)$, $J(t):=\partial_sH(s,t)|_{s=0}$, so that
$J(a)=J(b)=0$, and

$$L(s):=\int_a^b\sqrt{-g_{H(s,t)}\bigl(T(s,t),T(s,t)\bigr)}\,dt .$$

Then:

1. $L$ is differentiable at $0$ and
   $$L'(0)=-\int_a^b\frac{g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tJ(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}}\,dt =-\frac1c\int_a^bg_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tJ(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)\,dt .$$
2. Equivalently,
   $L'(0)=\frac1c\int_a^bg_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(J(t),D_t\gamma'(t)\bigr)\,dt$.
3. $L'(0)=0$ for **every** such variation $H$ if and only if
   $D_t\gamma'=0$ on $[a,b]$. Consequently, within this class, stationarity
   of the length functional is exactly the geodesic equation in the given
   proper-time parameter.

The chart hypothesis is used to realize variations of prescribed compactly
supported variation fields by coordinate displacement; the formula of claim 1
and the implication "geodesic $\Rightarrow$ stationary" are local and do not
require it beyond the smooth parametrization.
items.strategy: Differentiate the length functional of a two-parameter variation under the integral sign, commute the covariant derivatives D_s and D_t, integrate by parts with fixed endpoints, and use bump test fields to prove that stationarity for every variation is equivalent to the geodesic equation.

items.title: The Lorentzian Gauss lemma and the radial maximum of proper time
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $p\in M$.
Let $W_p\subseteq T_pM$ be a star-shaped open neighborhood of $0$ on which
$\exp_p$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open set $U_p:=\exp_p(W_p)$, as supplied
by [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] and
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]; identify
$T_v(T_pM)$ with $T_pM$ for every $v$.

**(a) Gauss lemma.** For every $v\in W_p$ and every $w\in T_pM$,

$$g_{\exp_pv}\bigl(d(\exp_p)_v(v),\,d(\exp_p)_v(w)\bigr)=g_p(v,w).$$

**(b) Radial maximum.** Let $\alpha:[0,1]\to U_p$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike curve with $\alpha(0)=p$, with nonzero future timelike one-sided
tangents, set $q:=\alpha(1)$ and $v_q:=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$. Then

$$L_g(\alpha)\le\sqrt{-g_p(v_q,v_q)},$$

and equality holds if and only if there are $v_0\in W_p$ and a piecewise-$C^1$
strictly increasing surjection $\rho:[0,1]\to[0,\rho(1)]$ with
$v_q=\rho(1)v_0$ and $\alpha(t)=\exp_p(\rho(t)v_0)$ for all $t$; that is,
$\alpha$ is a monotone reparametrization of the radial geodesic segment from
$p$ to $q$. Dividing by $c$, the proper-time increment of $\alpha$ is at most
$\frac1c\sqrt{-g_p(v_q,v_q)}$, which is the proper-time increment of that
radial geodesic.
items.strategy: Prove the Gauss identity g(d exp_p|_v v, d exp_p|_v w)=g_p(v,w) by the two-parameter family and D_s J = D_r T, then derive the radial proper-time maximum and its equality case from the reverse Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

items.title: Adopted clock, free-fall and light-ray assumptions of the classical gravitational framework
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the matter-content
assumptions of the framework, the following rules by which ideal clocks, test
bodies and light couple to the metric $g$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]].

**(i) Ideal clocks.** An **ideal clock** is an idealized physical device
carried along a future timelike worldline ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]])
whose readings are assumed to reproduce the proper time of that worldline:
the difference of two readings taken at two events of the worldline is the
proper-time increment between those events as defined by the metric, and it is
independent of the construction of the clock. Two ideal clocks moving along
the same worldline differ only by an additive constant (their choice of zero);
different worldlines generally accrue different proper times between the same
pair of events. The physical constant $c$ and the unit of duration are those
of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(ii) Free fall of massive test bodies.** A **test body** is an uncharged
idealized body whose internal structure is small compared with the scale over
which the geometry of the model varies and whose gravitational self-field is
negligible within the model. An **ideal freely falling massive test body** is
assumed to have a worldline that is a future timelike geodesic of the
metric-selected connection ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]), traversed with physical
four-velocity $U=d\gamma/d\tau$ satisfying
$g_{\gamma(\tau)}(U,U)=-c^2$; proper time is an affine parameter of the
worldline ([[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]). The
worldline is determined by the event at which the body is released together
with its four-velocity there, by the uniqueness of the geodesic initial-value
problem ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]); no force, charge, or
rest mass of the body enters this rule.

**(iii) Light rays.** In the geometric-optics approximation an **ideal light
ray** propagating in the model is assumed to be a future null geodesic of the
metric-selected connection
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]). A null worldline carries no proper
time and no four-velocity in the sense of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]; within the approximation the
propagation of an ideal ray is independent of its frequency, and only the
ray's direction in the tangent space is fixed, not a scale along it.

**(iv) Scope and exclusions.** The three rules are adopted in the test-field
regime of the smooth classical model: the clocks, bodies and rays do not
back-react on the geometry, and the geometry varies smoothly on the scales
relevant to them. Configurations requiring the body's own gravitational field,
radiation reaction, an electromagnetic or other self-force, finite-size or
tidal couplings beyond the test-body idealization, non-geometric-optics
propagation, dispersion or dissipation of light, or quantum effects are
outside these assumptions and require additional model content. The
assumptions do not assert that any real clock, body or light ray is exactly
ideal, nor do they attach measured readings to any model.
items.strategy: Adopt, and mark as adopted assumptions rather than derived results, the clock, free-fall and light-ray rules of the classical framework: ideal clocks measure proper time, ideal massive test bodies follow future timelike geodesics, and ideal light rays are future null geodesics in geometric optics, with the test-field regime and exclusions stated.
items.physical_scope: Adopted coupling assumptions of the classical smooth gravitational model: ideal clocks measure the proper time of their future timelike worldlines; ideal freely falling massive test bodies follow future timelike geodesics of the metric-selected connection; ideal light rays are future null geodesics in the geometric-optics approximation. The assumptions are stated in the test-field regime of the smooth four-dimensional model and exclude self-force and radiation back-reaction, finite-size and tidal couplings beyond the test-body idealization, non-geometric-optics propagation, dispersion and dissipation, matter with non-negligible gravitational self-field, distributional or lower-dimensional sources, and quantum effects. They are adopted assumptions of the framework, not derived or empirical results; empirical comparison belongs to fully specified models and reported observations.

items.title: The free-fall worldline of an ideal test body is determined by its initial event and four-velocity
items.statement:
Let a model of the classical gravitational framework be specified by a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ with its
metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and assume the
clock, free-fall and light-ray assumptions of
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$U_0\in T_pM$ be a future timelike unit vector,
$g_p(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]).

Suppose $B_1$ and $B_2$ are two ideal freely falling massive test bodies of
the model that are released at the event $p$ with physical four-velocity $U_0$:
their worldlines $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ pass through $p$ and their
four-vectors there equal $U_0$. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be their proper
times, with origins chosen so that $\gamma_1(0)=\gamma_2(0)=p$. Then
$\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ coincide wherever both are defined:

$$\gamma_1(\tau)=\gamma_2(\tau)\qquad\text{for every }\tau\text{ in the common domain}.$$

and each is the maximal timelike geodesic through $(p,U_0)$. In particular the
worldline of an ideal freely falling massive test body is determined by the
release event and the initial four-velocity alone; parameters that distinguish
the two bodies, such as their rest masses, do not enter.
items.strategy: Derive from the adopted free-fall rule and the unique maximal geodesic through (p,U_0) that two ideal freely falling massive test bodies released at the same event with the same four-velocity coincide, and that their common worldline is independent of rest mass and other body parameters.
items.physical_scope: Model-conditional statement within the classical smooth gravitational framework with its adopted clock, free-fall and light-ray assumptions: under the test-body idealization, two ideal freely falling massive test bodies released at the same event with the same physical four-velocity have the same worldline. It excludes bodies with non-negligible self-field, finite-size or tidal couplings beyond the idealization, self-force and radiation back-reaction, and quantum effects; it makes no empirical claim that all bodies in nature fall alike, and it does not establish the equivalence principle as a law of nature.

items.title: Scope of normal coordinates and of the local-inertial-frame reading
items.statement:
This remark separates the mathematics of
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] and
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] from the physical reading
usually attached to them, and is bookkeeping: it establishes no mathematical
result and no physical law.

- **What the construction gives.** For every event $p$ there is a chart with
  $g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$ and
  $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$, and in the exponential chart of an orthonormal
  basis the geodesics through $p$ are the straight coordinate lines through
  the origin
  ([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]). The identities
  are first order at the single point $p$.

- **What it does not give.** The construction asserts nothing about the second
  and higher derivatives of the metric, and therefore nothing about the
  curvature of the model; a chart of this kind is not an isometry and does not
  make any neighborhood of $p$ identical with a region of Minkowski space.
  The remark makes no curvature claim here; the second-order behavior is the
  subject of the curvature material of this track, which is a later page of
  the same category.

- **No global inertial frame, no congruence.** A chart with the normal-form
  identities at one event is not a global label of events by inertial
  coordinates, and the exponential charts at different points are not
  compatible frames. An "observer" in this library is a single future unit
  timelike vector at a point, and a "congruence" is a field of such vectors
  on an open set ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
  [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]); a freely falling
  observer is one timelike geodesic, not a global reference frame. Charts
  adapted to a congruence are a different construction from the normal
  coordinates of a geodesic through a point.

- **The physical reading is adopted, not derived.** The statement that an
  ideal freely falling test body or observer, using normal coordinates around
  an event of its own worldline, finds the local form of the metric to be that
  of Minkowski space at first order — and the associated local
  inertial-frame reading of the equivalence principle — depends on the
  adopted clock and free-fall assumptions of
  [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. It is a statement about the model in
  the test-body idealization, not a derivation from the geometry alone and not
  an empirical claim that real experiments cannot detect a gravitational
  field locally. The limitations recorded in the postulate — finite-size and
  tidal couplings of extended bodies, self-force, and nonlocal measurements —
  are precisely what the first-order identities cannot exclude.
items.strategy: Separate the first-order normal-coordinate mathematics from its physical reading: no second-order or neighborhood-flatness claim, no global inertial frame, no observer congruence, and no empirical equivalence-principle statement.
items.physical_scope: Scope note on the physical reading of point-normal and exponential coordinate charts: what the construction does and does not assert about local inertial frames, freely falling observers and the equivalence principle in the classical smooth model. Excludes global frames, neighborhood flatness, curvature claims, and any empirical equivalence-principle statement.

items.title: Geodesics, proper time and parallel transport of the flat model
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, the flat
Lorentzian metric $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the time orientation
$N=\partial_0$, so that $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Then:

1. The coordinate connection $\nabla$ with $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=0$ in the identity
   chart is the metric-selected connection of $g$, and its geodesics are
   exactly the affine lines $t\mapsto p+tv$.
2. For a geodesic with timelike tangent $v$, the proper-time increment over
   $[t_0,t]$ is $\sqrt{-g(v,v)}\,(t-t_0)/c$; in particular the future timelike
   geodesic through $p$ with four-velocity $u$ is
   $\tau\mapsto p+\tau u$, and its four-velocity $u$ has $g(u,u)=-c^2$.
3. Parallel transport by $\nabla$ along any piecewise smooth curve preserves
   the components in the identity chart: $D_tV=0$ if and only if $V$ has
   constant components; hence transport is a $g$-isometry, and the transported
   vector depends only on the endpoints.
4. The exponential map is $\exp_p(v)=p+v$ on all of $T_pM$, with
   $d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}$, and the identity chart translated to $p$
   gives $g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ exactly (not merely at
   first order).
items.strategy: On flat R^4 with the trivial coordinate connection, verify metric compatibility and torsion freedom to identify the metric-selected connection, then compute its geodesics, proper-time increments, parallel transport and exponential map explicitly.

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 3.3: the geodesic equation and proper time as an affine parameter in flat spacetime, printed pp. 37-38 (PDF pp. 38-39)

items.title: The metric-selected connection of a conformal metric, verified by the defining identities
items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open, let $\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, put
$\Omega:=e^{\varphi}>0$ and consider the conformal metric

$$g_{ab}=\Omega^2\,\eta_{ab}=e^{2\varphi}\eta_{ab},\qquad \eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1),$$

on $U$, with the identity chart and the time orientation $N=\partial_0$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Define, in this chart,

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}:=\delta^a{}_b\,\partial_c\varphi+\delta^a{}_c\,\partial_b\varphi-\eta_{bc}\,\eta^{ad}\partial_d\varphi .$$

Then:

1. $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\Gamma^a{}_{cb}$, so the resulting connection is
   torsion-free.
2. The compatibility identity
   $\partial_ag_{bc}=\sum_d\bigl(\Gamma^d{}_{ab}g_{dc}+\Gamma^d{}_{ac}g_{bd}\bigr)$
   holds identically on $U$.
3. By the uniqueness part of
   [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]], this connection
   is the metric-selected connection of $g$ on $U$; hence the displayed
   formula is the Levi–Civita connection of every conformally flat metric in
   these coordinates.

As a finite check, for the special choice $\varphi(x)=\lambda x^1$ the nonzero
symbols are $\Gamma^0{}_{01}=\Gamma^0{}_{10}=\lambda$,
$\Gamma^1{}_{00}=\lambda$ and $\Gamma^1{}_{11}=\lambda$, and the identity of
claim 2 is verified on the components $(a,b,c)=(1,0,0)$ and $(0,0,0)$ below.
items.strategy: Verify by direct computation that the displayed Christoffel symbols of a conformal metric are symmetric in the lower indices and satisfy the compatibility identity, conclude by uniqueness that they are the Levi-Civita coefficients, and check the identities on a finite special case.

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 3.2: the Christoffel formula (3.33), printed pp. 35-37 (PDF pp. 36-38)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.2.3: the Levi-Civita connection and its components (3.16)-(3.17), printed pp. 109-111 (PDF pp. 116-118)

items.title: A geodesic image with a non-affine parameter, and the equation of a pregeodesic
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart $x$, the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the metric-selected connection
$\nabla$, which in this chart has $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=0$; its geodesics are the
affine lines ([[ex-gr-flat-space-geodesics-and-proper-time]]).

1. The curve $\beta:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^4$,
   $\beta(s):=(s^2,0,0,0)$, has as image the positive half of the $x^0$-axis,
   which is the image of the affine geodesic $\gamma(\sigma):=(\sigma,0,0,0)$;
   nevertheless $\beta$ is not a geodesic in its own parameter, because
   $D_s\beta'(s)=(2,0,0,0)\neq0$ for every $s>0$.
2. The reparametrization is explicit: $\beta=\gamma\circ h$ with
   $h(s)=s^2$, and
   $D_s\beta'(s)=h''(s)\,\gamma'(h(s))=(2,0,0,0)$, in agreement with the
   general formula that a reparametrized geodesic is geodesic exactly for
   affine $h$ ([[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]], clause 4).
3. In the language of the pregeodesic equation, $\beta$ satisfies
   $\nabla_{\beta'}\beta'=f\beta'$ with $f(s)=1/s=h''(s)/h'(s)$; a curve with
   this property and $f$ continuous is the image of a geodesic, but its own
   parameter is not affine.
items.strategy: Exhibit beta(s)=(s^2,0,0,0), whose image is that of an affine geodesic but with D_s beta' nonzero, and compute the proportionality D_s beta' = f beta' with f = h''/h'.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: the geodesic equation (3.47), the affine freedom and the equation satisfied by a non-affine geodesic parameter, printed pp. 70-71 (PDF pp. 77-78)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 3.3: reparametrizations of a geodesic satisfy $\nabla_YY=fY$, and affine parameters form a two-parameter family, printed pp. 37-38 (PDF pp. 38-39)

items.title: Torsion-free connections with the same geodesic images need not coincide
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and its metric-selected connection
$
abla_0$. If a torsion-free affine connection $
abla'$ on $M$ has the same
geodesic images as $
abla_0$ — every regular curve is, up to
reparametrization, a geodesic of $
abla'$ if and only if it is one of
$
abla_0$ — then $
abla'=
abla_0$, and in particular $
abla'$ is
$g$-compatible" ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).
items.strategy: Refute the claim that torsion freedom plus geodesic images determine the connection with the torsion-free, non-metric-compatible connection Gamma'^a_bc = delta^a_b delta^0_c + delta^a_c delta^0_b, proving its geodesic images are exactly the straight lines by an ODE uniqueness argument.

items.title: The radial proper-time maximum checked on an explicit family of wiggly curves in flat space
items.statement:
Keep the flat model of [[ex-gr-flat-space-geodesics-and-proper-time]]:
$M=\mathbb R^4$ with the identity chart, $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$,
the metric-selected connection with $\Gamma=0$, and $c>0$. Fix
$0\le a<c/\pi$ and consider the piecewise smooth curve

$$\alpha_a:[0,1]\longrightarrow\mathbb R^4,\qquad \alpha_a(t):=\bigl(ct,\ a\sin(\pi t),\ 0,\ 0\bigr).$$

Its endpoints are $p=(0,0,0,0)$ and $q=(c,0,0,0)$, it has nonzero future
timelike tangents for every $t$, and it stays in the exponential domain
$\mathbb R^4$ of $p$, so [[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]]
applies with $v_q=\exp_p^{-1}(q)=(c,0,0,0)$. Then:

1. Its length is $L_g(\alpha_a)=\int_0^1\sqrt{c^2-a^2\pi^2\cos^2(\pi t)}\,dt$,
   and $L_g(\alpha_a)<c=\sqrt{-g(v_q,v_q)}$ for every $a\neq0$, while
   $L_g(\alpha_0)=c$.
2. Hence the curve is strictly below the radial maximum unless $a=0$, in which
   case $\alpha_0(t)=(ct,0,0,0)$ is the radial geodesic itself (a straight
   line through $p$); this exhibits the equality case of the theorem on an
   explicit family.
items.strategy: Evaluate the radial maximum theorem on the family alpha_a(t)=(ct, a sin(pi t), 0, 0): compute the length integral, obtain strict inequality for a != 0 from monotonicity over a nondegenerate subinterval, and exhibit the equality case a = 0.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3: the proper-time variational argument and the maximum property of timelike geodesics, printed pp. 69-73 (PDF pp. 76-80)
D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), the twin-paradox discussion of the maximal proper time of inertial worldlines, printed pp. 30-33 (PDF pp. 37-40)

items.title: A chart with the point-normal first-order form whose second metric derivatives do not vanish
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "If a smooth chart $(U,x)$ of a smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold satisfies the point-normal first-order identities
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$ at a
point $p\in U$, then in addition $\partial_a\partial_bg_{cd}(p)=0$"
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).
items.strategy: Refute the second-order vanishing claim with the metric eta_ab + (x^0)^2 delta^1_a delta^1_b on R^4, whose identity chart satisfies the point-normal first-order identities at 0 while partial_0 partial_0 g_11(0) = 2 != 0.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.3.2: it is not generally possible to make the second derivatives of the metric vanish in normal coordinates, with the parameter-counting argument, printed pp. 119-121 (PDF pp. 126-128)
